title: The analysis tree

D0.outcome: Explains the analysis tree: each branch is examined once, its end-verdict noted, and only then is a move chosen.

D1.outcome: Draws a tree for three candidates with two replies each to four plies and gives a one-word verdict at each end.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, builds the tree without revisiting the same branch, and reaches the same verdict as the engine check on at least 7 of 10 positions.

D3.outcome: In positions with many forcing replies, prunes by forcing moves first, notes transpositions, and records the result so a branch is not recomputed.

misconceptions: Jumping between branches is a sign of thoroughness (it is the usual cause of missed lines).
A deeper tree is a better tree.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S4 (Kotov, Aagaard, Ramesh, Dvoretsky, Rowson, Heisman, all [R] in the map)
docs/council-synthesis.md Round 3 (Kotov: each branch once; Aagaard: avoid repeated rechecking)
sources/sheets/emlasker_common-sense.md §4.13 (analysis by plans, not trees; completeness claims suspect)
conditions: Used when the position is concrete enough that branches end in a clear verdict within about four plies.
Plan enumeration works when the number of strategic plans is small, but a claim that no other plan exists is rarely provable.
contrasts: Rechecking the same branch in the same order (thinking inertia).
Declaring that the enumerated plans are all the plans, and missing an extra resource.
A quiet position where branches never end in a verdict.
